review_notes.root_cause_and_reference: The fork commit f1b7aebff8c2 is cited correctly. Upstream llvmorg-20.1.8 RISCVInstrInfoXCV.td:427-430 defines cv.extract/cv.extractu.{h,b}. Its :792-795 selects the sign-extending instruction for sext_inreg and the zero-extending instruction for the and-0xff/0xffff form (CV_EXTBZ/CV_EXTHZ). The fix follows the same rule. GAP9 GCC -O2 emits pv.extractu.b for an unsigned char lane, pv.extract.b for a signed char lane and pv.extractu.h for an unsigned short lane, which matches the new selection.
review_notes.semantics_encoding: GVSoC isa_pulpv2.py:288-291 and pulp_v2.hpp/int.h lib_VEC_EXTU_8/16 mask and shift with no sign extension. lib_VEC_EXT_8/16 cast through int8_t/int16_t, so they sign-extend. The fork .td uses funct5 0b10010 for extractu and 0b01111 for extract. llvm-mc and GAP9 gas produce identical bytes: pv.extractu.b a0,a1,3 = 0x9215f557, pv.extractu.h a0,a1,1 = 0x9205e557, pv.extract.b = 0x7a15f557, pv.extract.h = 0x7a05e557. These agree with the GVSoC decode masks.
review_notes.other_paths: The fork has no C++ code that touches EXTRACT_VECTOR_ELT, AssertZext or computeKnownBits for the PULP types (grep of RISCVISelLowering.cpp, RISCVISelDAGToDAG.cpp and PULP/). The generic DAG treats the upper bits of an extract wider than its element as any-extended: computeKnownBits leaves them unknown and ComputeNumSignBits returns 1. So the plain vector_extract to PV_EXTRACT pattern (any-extend) is valid. A zext always reaches ISel as the and-mask form, which is fixed. The variable-index path (pv.shuffle.b/h then p.extbz/p.exthz/p.extbs/p.exths) is correct. The dotp fragments (uhextract/shextract) map to dotup/dotusp/dotsp, whose signedness is correct and which this commit does not change. With my IR cases (logs/20-F029-review/ir.ll) at llc -O0/-O1/-O2/-O3 every function selects correctly: zext to i16 then store, icmp ult/slt/eq on i8 and i16 lanes, zext to i64, sext i8->i16 then zext to i32 (pv.extract.b + p.exthz), variable-index zext/sext, trunc of an i16 lane to i8 then zext/sext (pv.extract.h + p.extbz/p.extbs), lane 5 of <8 x i8>, select and add.
